findings.F1: The tested situation is too narrow to trade: on the 5-day grid of folds B and C it gives only 5 cases on 5 days, so the book made 32 trades at 0.004 trades a day and was in a position on 1 % of coin-days. In the same choppy, agitated profile, dropping the 20-day band (a close in the upper half of the range after a negative 5-day return, with any 20-day fall) gives 17 cases on 10 days with a mean short-direction unusual 5-day move of +15.7 % (t 2.26).
findings.F2: The deepest 20-day falls, which the idea's consequence leaves out, carry the most. Among profile closes in the upper half after a negative 5-day return, the mean 5-day short-direction move is +21.5 % (10 cases, t 3.02, 6 days) when the 20-day return is below -20 %. It is +10.2 % for 5 cases between -20 % and -10 %, and +0.0 % for 2 cases between -10 % and 0. In the book, trades entered with a 20-day return below -15 % averaged +5.6 % net (13 trades), against -6.2 % (19 trades) for the rest.

ideas.idea: In a choppy, agitated market, when a coin's daily close sits in the upper part of that day's high-low range after its 5-day return has been negative, its price falls over the next five days, and the nearer that close is to the day's high and the deeper its 20-day fall, the larger the fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader shorts these high closes after any 20-day fall and sizes the short up as the 20-day fall deepens, instead of keeping only falls of a tenth to a fifth.
ideas.name: high close fades, deeper falls

ideas.idea: In a choppy, agitated market, when a coin's daily close sits in the upper part of that day's high-low range, its price falls over the next five days, and the deeper its 5-day fall before that close and the nearer the close is to the high, the larger the fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader shorts high closes in a choppy, agitated market by the depth of the coin's 5-day fall, which gives more cases than the tested 20-day band.
ideas.name: high close after drop fades

ideas.idea: In a choppy, agitated market, when a coin's daily close sits in the upper part of that day's high-low range after its 5-day return has been negative, its price falls over the next ten days, and the nearer that close is to the day's high, the larger the fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader holds the short on these high closes for ten days rather than five.
ideas.name: high close fades over ten days
